description: K3S local deployment verification — deploy ClawManager to a local k3d cluster on macOS and verify the admin portal is accessible at https://localhost:30443
acceptance_criteria: k3d cluster created successfully
All pods in clawmanager-system namespace are Running
Admin portal accessible at https://localhost:30443
Admin can log in with default credentials
steps: Create k3d cluster with port mapping 30443
Wait for all pods to be Running
evidence_hint: kubectl get pods -n clawmanager-system (all Running) + screenshot of admin login page

description: Multi-OpenClaw instance scheduling — use ClawManager to create 2 OpenClaw instances on the local K3S cluster and verify both are accessible simultaneously
acceptance_criteria: Can create instance from admin portal
K3S schedules a Pod within 30 seconds
Both instances are Running at the same time
Each instance has a unique access URL/token
User can connect to both instances via browser
steps: Verify both pods Running in K3S
evidence_hint: kubectl get pods -n clawmanager-<user-id> (2 pods Running) + screenshots of both desktop sessions

description: User authentication full chain — verify admin and user login, JWT token flow, role-based access control (admin vs regular user), and session expiry
acceptance_criteria: Admin can log in and access admin-only pages
Regular user can log in and only see their own instances
JWT token expires after configured duration
Invalid credentials return 401
steps: Create admin account and regular user account
Test admin login and verify admin-only routes accessible
Test user login and verify user-only sees own instances
evidence_hint: API test results showing 401/403 on unauthorized access

description: Instance lifecycle management — start, stop, and delete instances through the ClawManager UI and verify K3S Pod state changes accordingly
acceptance_criteria: Stop instance → Pod is terminated/suspended
Start stopped instance → Pod is recreated and Running
Delete instance → Pod and PVC are cleaned up
Instance status in UI reflects actual K3S state
steps: Stop it via UI, verify pod state
Start it via UI, verify pod Running again
Delete it via UI, verify pod and PVC gone
evidence_hint: kubectl get pods/pvc before and after each operation

description: AI Gateway basic configuration — configure at least one LLM provider (e.g., local Ollama or OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and verify AI features work through the gateway
acceptance_criteria: AI Gateway config page accessible in admin portal
Can add an LLM provider with API key
Test request routes through gateway successfully
Audit log records the request
steps: Navigate to AI Gateway in admin portal
evidence_hint: Screenshot of successful gateway test response + audit_logs table entry
